title: The Grade Margin Kept Standing Under a Warehouse Receipt
content:
The grade the grain is standing at is kept in view when a receipt is reduced, since a receipt names a grade and has to be redeemable in it. This rule governs warehouse receipts issued against Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The governing terms

Where the grade of record stands below US No. 2 and the agreement guarantees the grade written on the receipt, the wide grade margin of 900 bushels is kept.

Where the grade of record stands at US No. 2 or above and a grade discount has been raised on the account in the last twelve months, the light grade margin of 300 bushels is kept.

And otherwise no grade margin is kept.

## What counts as standing below US No. 2

A grade of record of US No. 3 or of sample grade stands below US No. 2. A grade of record of US No. 2 or better does not.

## The grade each programme guarantees

| Programme | Grade guaranteed |
| --- | --- |
| Open Storage Account | house average grade |
| Grain Bank Deposit Account | house average grade |
| Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage | receipt grade |
| Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement | receipt grade |
| Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement | receipt grade |
| Identity Preserved Segregated Storage | delivered lot grade |

## Condition and result

| Grade of record | The agreement guarantees the grade written on the receipt | A grade discount raised on the account in the last twelve months | Margin kept |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| below US No. 2 | yes | either way | 900 |
| below US No. 2 | no | either way | none |
| US No. 2 or above | either way | yes | 300 |
| US No. 2 or above | either way | no | none |

The two lines do not overlap: the first turns only on a grade below US No. 2, the second only on a grade at US No. 2 or above.

## Worked margins, on hypothetical agreements

**A Commercial Warehouse Receipt Storage whose grade of record is US No. 3.** The grade stands below US No. 2 and the programme guarantees the grade written on the receipt, so 900 bushels are kept.

**An Open Storage Account whose grade of record is sample grade.** The grade stands below US No. 2, but that programme guarantees the house average grade rather than the receipt grade, so no grade margin is kept.

**A Conditioned Reserve Storage Agreement whose grade of record is US No. 1, with a grade discount raised on the account four months ago.** The grade stands above US No. 2 and a discount stands within the twelve months, so 300 bushels are kept.
